title: Controlled odd/even frequency bucketing and harmonic anomaly testing
summary: Two recorded or synthetic voices can be spectrally interleaved across 100 Hz bins as a positive synthetic example; applying the same masks to a field recording changes listening views and is not evidence of provenance or deliberate composition.
invariants: Preserve immutable original recordings and transformations with parameters and SHA-256 authority; do not publish minors or private recordings.
Source, channel, spectral view, apparent speech and speaker attribution are separate concepts.
Odd/even complementary masks recombine the original passband; this is an identity, not a proof of two sources.
A missing harmonic is neither necessary nor sufficient to demonstrate multiple digitally interleaved speech streams.
f0 must be estimated on voiced broadband control material, not inferred independently for each narrow band.
Fixed-gain spectral views and nonlinear quiet-pass reinforcement are separate transformations.
Comparative human transcriptions are hypotheses; blind listening, natural overlap and codec/traffic controls are mandatory before escalation.
Audio V9 source/family and Job-to-Node/Storage Fabric authority boundaries remain unchanged.
procedure: Create a synthetic positive control Y(f)=M_even(f)A(f)+M_odd(f)B(f), alongside original A, B and A+B.
Record exact bucket widths, sampling rate, input hashes, channel geometry, bit depth and playback level.
For unknown X(f), emit separate odd/even listening views and fixed relative-preference variants; retain original stereo.
Compare against close-speech, natural overlap, wind, impacts, codec and playback negative controls.
Score voiced harmonic predictions with external f0 and local spectral evidence; do not infer number of sources from missing peaks.
Hold transcription, origin, motive and attribution separately, recording alternatives and uncertainty.
